the transcription factors DLX1/2 are required for the specification of the growth-promoting GHRH-neuron identity in the hypothalamus.
Dlx1 and Otp coordinate specification of the two function-specific neuronal subtypes in the ARC, GHRH neurons that control growth and AgRP neurons that regulate feeding and energy balance.
the transcription factors DLX1/2 and OTP coordinate the balanced generation and specification of GHRH-neuron and AgRP-neuron in the ARC.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the mechanisms that control neuronal specification and differentiation.
the molecular mechanisms that control hypothalamic development and function, and the genetic basis of growth disorders and obesity.
the molecular mechanisms of hypothalamic development.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
Dlx1/Otp are required for balanced generation of GHRH and AgRP neurons, and Dlx1/Otx2 are required for the specification of GHRH neuron identity.
Dlx1/Otp is required for GHRH neuron specification and suppresses AgRP neuron fate.
Dlx1 and 2 are required for the development of GHRH neurons and for suppressing AgRP neuronal fate.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
Dlx1-2 are essential for specifying GHRH-neuron identity, and that Dlx2 directly represses Otp to suppress AgRP-neuron fate.
Dlx1-2 and Otp are crucial for specifying GHRH-neuron identity, and simultaneously suppressing AgRP-neuron fate.
Dlx1 and Otp are required to coordinate the development of AgRP-neurons and GHRH neurons in the ARC.
The main takeaway from our work is that
Dlx1-2 and Otp act as a pair of antagonistic transcription factors to coordinate the development of these two functionally related ARC neurons.
